title: Make the documentation tree human-readable and human-editable
status_detail: Explicitly selected as the immediate documentation-migration priority and coordinating through active first child docs.human-readable.contract-and-inventory. Automatic successor activation remains disabled, and every later child still requires separate explicit activation.
objective: Establish docs/ as an ordinary human-authored, human-readable, human-editable documentation tree while relocating generated harness projections outside docs/ and preserving authoritative project, scientific, and historical content.
authorized_scope: Coordinate seven serial child Tasks covering the documentation contract and inventory, generated-view separation, root navigation, architecture and development navigation, computational-document renaming, current-versus-history separation, and final cutover.
Require every maintained docs/ page to be directly editable source, with obvious index-driven navigation and descriptive filenames, while keeping generated harness state outside docs/.
Preserve scientific definitions, results, provenance, durable decisions, publication records, and Git history while changing documentation ownership, paths, navigation, and generated-view placement.
completion_criteria: All seven child Tasks are complete under their separately activated scopes, docs/ contains no generated harness projections, and human-authored documentation is readable directly from the repository checkout.

Every first-level maintained documentation section has an obvious index, maintained links resolve, Sphinx passes with warnings as errors, and harness validation passes after generated-view relocation.
The completed documentation contract states that ordinary prose edits use edit, documentation validation, review, commit, and push without harness synchronization.
exclusions: Do not activate this parent or any child merely because this chain exists; do not enable automatic successor activation.
Do not change scientific meaning, calculation inputs or results, dependencies, lockfiles, release state, publication claims, protected-execution authority, or execute scientific software.
Do not delete retained evidence or historical material solely to simplify navigation; classify and preserve it under an explicit authoritative or historical owner.
